task: Core #1186 F6-U03i: complete isolated Docker PostgreSQL17 atomic 59-file baseline replay and rollback proof without hosted execution

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Critical isolated transaction proof only: approved immutable 59 reviewed source blobs and 4 companions, real Docker PostgreSQL17, source-authentic preflight/seed/postflight. No hosted connection, schema reset, endpoint identity, provider-backed Auth/Storage or signed-in RLS is authorized.

acceptanceCriteria: 59 migration SQL files exactly match the REVIEWED_SOURCE_COMMIT Git blob ids and canonical list, with 0001 start and 0058 terminal and both 0026 entries.
Emitted fresh-only SQL opens one transaction before source target-preflight, applies all 59 untouched migrations, auth-bootstrap, neutral seed, and source target-postflight before COMMIT.

PostgreSQL17 Docker service host/port/peer, local DB name and role are verified with no inherited PG*/DATABASE_URL/SUPABASE_DB_URL selectors; neither workflow nor composer accesses network/hybrid hosted credentials.
Successful 59-file local replay has preflight and postflight PASS, key app objects and expected final Office SQL functions; after commit, atomically persisted schema proven via read-only query.

An injection before COMMIT intentionally aborts the same 59-file transaction on a second fresh local database with 0 app-owned public/private relations, functions and policies afterward; guard reports TEST_ABORT_EXPECTED, not a success without rollback.
Every dry-run/negative/positive report explicitly disclaims hosted reset authorization, managed Auth/Storage, TLS identity and authenticated tenant RLS.
Run exact-head real PG17 workflow and all required canonical CI/Truth/Lifecycle gates to close scoped unit only.
invariants: All 59 original approved migration and companion SQL bytes are identical to reviewed commit; no security guard altered to make a test pass.
Source-only compiler cannot invoke psql, libpq, network, Docker or Supabase; CI executes exclusively a verified Docker PG17 local database.
F6-U03b original hosted compiler hard stops with FRESH_REPROVISION_HOSTED_EXECUTION_NOT_AUTHORIZED before DROP SCHEMA, unchanged and tested.
Preflight before first migration, postflight after all migration files and neutral seed and before COMMIT in one transaction.
Fault injection happens before COMMIT and uses a separate local fixture target; SQL fails and rollback empties only app-owned schemas.
Any real original SQL replay failure is BLOCKED; do not fabricate pass, substitute SQL, weaken original migrations or omit failures.
forbiddenStates: Running, connecting or sending any SQL to waterk-platform, waterk-staging or hosted Fresh Install.
Any shell, code, SQL or CI path that removes the hosted review abort or modifies migration content instead of reporting failure.
A local 59-file pass used to imply managed Supabase provider, TLS endpoint or authenticated Alap/Pro access proof.
Fault injection produces success without test exit failure, or test's public/private app schema is nonempty after rollback.
57/58/59 hand-picked SQL files pass as '59' without reviewed list identity, companion postflight or real transaction.

failureModes: One of 0055–0058 Office/RLS SQL statements depends on real Supabase provider internals, requiring an explicit diagnostic blocker instead of a fake shim pass.
The fresh target already has a public function, causing target-preflight to abort; no unconditional DROP may be used.
Migration 0026 is missing one of the two source files but totals are misreported.
psql returns zero after ignored individual SQL errors; force ON_ERROR_STOP=1 and fail the whole CI proof.
Injected fault occurs after COMMIT and cannot establish rollback integrity.
CI connection is redirected through libpq environment to a hosted database.
Postflight does not inspect some newly added Office object while the test incorrectly claims production readiness.
edgeCases: 59 files but 0058 is stale or modified compared to the source-reviewed Git commit.
Role/syntax mismatch in provider mock causes RLS creation failure on 0048+, preserving the failure artifact.
Rollback DB shares the same postgres:17 server but is isolated from the successfully committed fresh DB.
Functions created before abort persist due to unintentional autocommit, so rollback count must include relations, functions and policies.
Seed is deliberately customer-neutral and must never create a user profile or business tenant.
Storage/auth bootstrap trigger has dependencies on auth.users local shim; no claim it proves managed Auth API.
Review-only compiler includes intentional exception before DROP; tests must check its exact placement even though fresh-local composer has no DROP.

specialistReviews.finding: A local replay can be mistaken for hosted reset authorization; actual Docker redirection may target a remote DB.
specialistReviews.resolution: No connection code inside compiler, no libpq selectors inherited, verify real Docker IP and database, and retain hosted abort-before-DROP with negative tests.

specialistReviews.finding: A green migration count does not prove atomic persistence or rollback.
specialistReviews.resolution: One BEGIN/COMMIT for complete 59 and postflight; separate injected fault after postflight before COMMIT, assert no app-owned object state afterward.

specialistReviews.finding: A new duplicate guard or independent source selector could drift away from canonical reviewed baseline.
specialistReviews.resolution: Call the existing validateReviewedBaseline for migration list and content verification; preserve original F6-U03f authority and existing CI/Truth gates.

specialistReviews.finding: Docker PG17 does not supply hosted Auth/Storage event triggers or prove customer login and RLS integration.
specialistReviews.resolution: Result is labeled ONLY as local source + transaction scope; remaining hosted, provider and tenant-authenticated truth stays BLOCKED.

challenge.scenario: Source 0058 has changed but 59 filenames still match.
challenge.finding: A filename-count gate can pass a modified RLS guard migration.
challenge.resolution: Use existing source-reviewed Git blob byte verifier for all 59 plus companions and record digest.

challenge.finding: App migrations could overwrite non-empty customer target.
challenge.resolution: Original target-preflight must fail before first migration; never run DROP against occupied database.

challenge.scenario: Fault injection is after COMMIT or outside transaction.
challenge.finding: Rollback test creates irreversible schema changes.
challenge.resolution: Compile a second copy with an exception inserted before COMMIT; assert database app schemas empty after psql fails.

challenge.scenario: psql ON_ERROR_STOP is disabled or exit status ignored.
challenge.finding: Partial schema may be reported as successful full baseline.
challenge.resolution: Use ON_ERROR_STOP=1, explicit exit code checking and independent post-commit persistent object queries.

challenge.scenario: Container endpoint resolves to another PostgreSQL instance.
challenge.finding: A 59-file SQL test could target an unapproved environment.
challenge.resolution: Compare docker inspect peer IP, local DB, postgres role and version 17; disallow env selectors.

challenge.scenario: One test simulates historical 47 files then subsequent 12 as two commits.
challenge.resolution: Validate one and only one BEGIN/COMMIT enclosing all 59 and postflight.

challenge.scenario: Provider bootstrap shim overstates Auth/Storage behavior.
challenge.finding: Fake managed provider closure despite Docker-only run.
challenge.resolution: Persist explicit hostedFalse/providerFalse/JwtFalse scope fields; no RLS runtime claim.

challenge.scenario: All original SQL runs but postflight fails and test ignores it.
challenge.resolution: Full original postflight is included before commit with ON_ERROR_STOP and forced failure if any condition fails.

A local-only single BEGIN/COMMIT PostgreSQL17 transaction runs authentic target-preflight, all 59 source SQL files in reviewed order, auth-bootstrap, neutral seed and target-postflight, with independent exact target DB, role, version and actual Docker peer checks.

A separate clean Docker database receives an injected postflight-after-migrations fault inside the same 59-file transaction and demonstrably rolls back all application tables, functions and policies, rather than misreporting success.

Canonical Plan Before Code, Development Guard, Edit-Time/Incremental Replay, Quality, TS, Build, Completion Truth and Lifecycle evidence are required.
